title: `ward status` and `ward doctor`: safe state and read-only health reporting
description: Spec section 8's command table lists two commands that no WCLI task owned: 'ward status --json' (safe current-project and backend state; no global inventory or secret previews) and 'ward doctor --json' (read-only permissions, key-provider, schema, binding and instruction health; never dump keys or request headers). Filed at opum-agent's ruling (2026-09-28) after WCLI-7's session surfaced the gap, as one task because both are read-only reporting over the same project/binding/vault state. Scope: both commands and their contract tests. Non-goals: profile readiness reporting is 'ward check' (WCLI-9); operational events are 'ward audit' (WCLI-11).

acceptanceCriteria.text: Both commands are registered in the CLI contract (help and manifest) and emit the {schemaVersion, kind, data} envelope when passed --json; the contract test enumerates them

`ward status --json` reports the current project state — manifest/binding presence and project id, vault presence, key-provider reachability, schema version — and nothing outside the current project: no alias list, no secret name, value, length or fingerprint, no other project records; asserted by tests over a store seeded with sentinel values in this and another project (T09/T11 discipline)

`ward doctor --json` runs each check read-only — permissions, key-provider, schema, binding, instruction/bridge health — reports per-check results with stable safe codes, exits 0 when every check passes and 6 when any check fails while the others still report; a simulated single-check failure is asserted for each check

Neither command mutates state (vault, keychain, manifest and bridge files byte-identical before and after) and neither emits key material or request headers, asserted by sentinel and before/after byte-comparison tests
